title: Yuman EA agent contract
description: Schema for agent.yaml. Agents are few and stable; skills are many and contributed. If a routine contribution requires editing a file validated by this schema, the design is wrong. Two agent layers exist and they are shaped differently: L0 routes and never runs methods, L1 owns a domain and delegates to skills.

id.description: The router is 'orchestrator'. Every other agent is '<domain>-ea'. New agents require an ADR (CLAUDE.md anti-pattern 6).

description.description: WHEN to reach for this agent — the delegation trigger, in the words a user would use. Distinct from role, which says what the agent is responsible for: a host routes on this string and knows nothing else about the agent. Mirrored into AGENT.md frontmatter; see spec/standard-mapping.md.

layer.description: l0 = orchestration, exactly one agent. l1 = domain ownership. L2 subagents are not described by this schema.

role.description: One sentence. What this agent is responsible for, in functional language.

domain.description: Required for l1. Must agree with the id prefix.

owns_questions.description: Questions this agent answers, phrased as a practitioner would ask them. CI flags overlap across agents: the failure mode in multi-agent EA systems is never 'no agent answered', it is 'three agents answered differently'.

refuses.description: Declarative, machine-checkable boundaries. An agent that refuses nothing will eventually answer everything.

route_to.description: Where it goes instead. A route to an agent that does not exist yet is a CI error, not a placeholder.

available.description: False when the target agent is not yet shipped. The agent must then say so plainly rather than answering out of scope.

skills.description: Skill IDs or domain globs this agent may invoke. L1 only — the orchestrator does not hold skills.

subagents.description: L2 workers available for fan-out and context isolation.

escalates_to.description: L1 escalates to the orchestrator. Required for l1.

responsibilities.description: L0 only, and exactly these five. The list is closed because every addition is orchestrator bloat wearing a business case.

routes_to.description: L0 only. The domain agents that actually exist in this release.

on_unroutable.description: L0 only. 'answer_directly' is present so it can be rejected: choosing it is the definition of orchestrator bloat and CI rejects it.

non_goals.description: Stated in the agent's own prompt, not just here. Closed enum: these are the observed failure modes, and an agent that wants a novel non-goal probably wants an ADR.

context_slices.description: The enterprise context this agent is permitted to read and pass down. Naming it narrows what ends up in a context window.

evals.description: Agent-level golden cases. The orchestrator's routing eval is mandatory — see lifecycle.md R16.
